# term: # 0.3.0: missing from the order is not a defect (guide rule 1); kept, unmapped.
# The shipped list had 15 safety terms and no Tagalog hazard vocabulary.
# These 42 were already vetted in research/lexicons/mining_seeds_v1.tsv.
# Round 1 human labels: safety recall 0.593 -> 0.741 (in-sample; see
# research/hazard_tagger_measurement.json). Mild heat terms stay severity 2 so
# safety_false_friends_v1.tsv can suppress them in comfort/feature contexts.
# Completes the overheat/overheated/overheating family. Added after round 1
# showed "overheats" missed; disclosed as an in-sample addition.
# Model 0.3.0 additions (29 Sept 2026). Taken from the "typical words" lists in
# reviewers use; checked against labelling round 1 (in-sample) and against
# unlabelled reviews outside rounds 1 and 2. Round 2 is the held-out test.
# Hyphenated and spaced spellings normalize differently ("nag-on" -> "nagon"),
# so both are listed where both occur.
# Battery that drains fast (guide: "mabilis maubos ang battery").
# Counterfeit (guide: "hindi original, di orig, not genuine, iba sa picture").
# Electronic-gadgets scope expansion (15 Oct 2026). Two sources: confirmed
# project vetted from its own tagging guide but never fully shipped -- each
# AFFIX_PREFIXES first so no row here duplicates an existing lemma fold, e.g.
# "hindi nag-charge" was skipped because it already folds to shipped "hindi
# nagchacharge"); and gaps specific to gadget subcategories with real scraped
# review data (earbuds, keyboard/mouse, controllers, CCTV/smart home).
# ~6,020 labelled sentences) and against ~14,000 freshly-scraped unlabelled
# reviews (real-text spot checks, no ground truth there). Dropped from the
# original candidate list after measurement/spot-checking: "hindi tugma"
# (15 of 16 labelled hits wrong -- it means "doesn't match/fit" in size,
# colour or a physical part, not counterfeit); bare "black screen" (matched
# a review describing the reviewer's OLD, DIFFERENT device, not this
# product); bare "double click" (matched an earbud's "double-click the power
# button to turn off the light" instruction, not a mouse defect -- the
# gerund/verb-marked forms below don't collide with that phrasing). "di
# original" kept despite one labelled miss (a hypothetical-fear sentence):
# it mirrors already-shipped "hindi original"/"hindi orig", so the miss
# reflects an existing, already-accepted speculation-guard limitation, not
# new risk. Several Tier C candidates (stick drift, cursor not moving,
# sticky keys, "static" noise, bare "signal", CCTV blurry-footage
# reclassification) were investigated and explicitly NOT added: no real
# occurrences to measure against (controller/CCTV subcategories have no
# dedicated scrape yet), or the evidence was mixed/risky (bare "signal" hit
# positive uses like "Stable signal, no more dropped calls!"; "static" had
# only 1 right vs 1 wrong on the one small labelled sample available). This
# addition requires the hazard_classifier_v6 learned model (safety, defect)
# to be rebuilt, since its keyword_file_hashes() check locks it to the
# lexicon content it was trained with.
